chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, from Ali al-Asraq, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) - Ali (peace be upon him) - at his death, said: 'O Ali, the farmers will not be wronged in your presence, and no extra tax will be taken on land upon which a tax has been fixed, and no corvée (forced labor/service) will be imposed on a Muslim.''
From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to write to his governors: 'Do not impose corvée on the Muslims, and whoever asks you for more than the fixed tax, he has transgressed, so do not give him.' And he used to write: 'I advise regarding the farmers, that they be treated well, and they are the farmers (karrun).'
ai.seo_question: What were the rules regarding land tax and forced labor for Muslims according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from Tahdhib al-Ahkam highlights the Prophet’s final testament to Imam Ali regarding equitable land tax (kharaj) and the prohibition of forced labor (sukhrah) on Muslims, a principle Imam Ali rigorously applied through his directives to provincial governors. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on administrative justice, ensuring that fiscal policies do not burden the agricultural class beyond the obligatory dues, thereby preventing arbitrary exactions by officials.
